title: A Predictor That Learns from Error

scenes.tts: Damage the cerebellum, and a person can still move. So what is lost?
scenes.visual: Title card fades. A side view of the brain; the cerebellum, at the back under the cerebral hemispheres, glows. The question appears beside it.
scenes.narration: Damage the cerebellum, and a person can still move. So what is lost?

scenes.tts: Watch someone with cerebellar damage reach for a cup.
scenes.visual: Two arms side by side reach for two identical cups. Left label: healthy. Right label: cerebellar damage.
scenes.narration: Watch someone with cerebellar damage reach for a cup.

scenes.tts: Is the movement weak, or clumsy? And where does it go most wrong?
scenes.visual: Both reaches freeze mid-way. On screen: Weak, or clumsy? Where does it go most wrong?
scenes.narration: Is the movement weak, or clumsy? And where does it go most wrong?

scenes.tts: Clumsy, not weak. The reach overshoots, and the hand shakes as it nears the cup.
scenes.visual: The healthy hand lands cleanly. The other overshoots the cup, then oscillates around it; a small zigzag trace of its path draws beside it. Label: overshoot, shaking near the target.
scenes.narration: Clumsy, not weak. The reach overshoots, and the hand shakes as it nears the cup.

scenes.tts: Feedback is slow. A visual error arrives a tenth of a second or more after the movement went wrong.
scenes.visual: A timeline: a command leaves the brain at time zero; the arm moves; the visual report of the error arrives later, marked: 0.1 s or more.
scenes.narration: Feedback is slow. A visual error arrives a tenth of a second or more after the movement went wrong.

scenes.tts: In one model, a hand steered by late feedback, with strong corrections, overshoots and swings.
scenes.visual: A hand driven by the delayed report with strong corrections: each correction arrives late, and the path swings back and forth across the target. Small label: one model, delayed feedback plus strong corrections; one proposed contributor.
scenes.narration: In one model, a hand steered by late feedback, with strong corrections, overshoots and swings.

scenes.tts: So the cerebellum predicts. It estimates what a command will do, before the senses report the result.
scenes.visual: Definition card: Prediction = the brain's estimate of what a command will do, made before the senses report the result.
scenes.narration: So the cerebellum predicts. It estimates what a command will do, before the senses report the result.

scenes.tts: To learn a prediction, you need two things. A description of what is happening. And a signal that says wrong.
scenes.visual: Two empty slots appear: Context, and Error.
scenes.narration: To learn a prediction, you need two things. A description of what is happening. And a signal that says wrong.

scenes.tts: Mossy fibres bring the context, including a copy of the commands the cortex is sending.
scenes.visual: A schematic builds: blue mossy fibres rise from the pons, labelled copy of the command from cortex; others from spinal cord and vestibular nuclei, labelled what the body senses.
scenes.narration: Mossy fibres bring the context, including a copy of the commands the cortex is sending.

scenes.tts: Granule cells relay it as parallel fibres, which run like telephone wires through many Purkinje cells.
scenes.visual: Blue parallel fibres stream sideways through a row of flat, fan-shaped Purkinje dendrites, like wires through trees. The Context slot fills.
scenes.narration: Granule cells relay it as parallel fibres, which run like telephone wires through many Purkinje cells.

scenes.tts: In the classical model, one climbing fibre carries the error, from the inferior olive. Each adult Purkinje cell gets just one.
scenes.visual: A single red climbing fibre rises from the inferior olive and winds up one Purkinje dendrite. The Error slot fills, labelled: teaching signal, classical model.
scenes.narration: In the classical model, one climbing fibre carries the error, from the inferior olive. Each adult Purkinje cell gets just one.

scenes.tts: Purkinje cells are the only output of the cerebellar cortex, and they inhibit. They press a brake on the deep or vestibular nuclei.
scenes.visual: A grey deep-nucleus cell below; the Purkinje axon ends on it with a minus sign. A brake pedal icon sits on the connection.
scenes.narration: Purkinje cells are the only output of the cerebellar cortex, and they inhibit. They press a brake on the deep or vestibular nuclei.

scenes.tts: Many nuclear cells fire steadily, like a car with its engine running. Ease off the brake, and the car speeds up.
scenes.visual: The nucleus cell fires a steady train of ticks. The brake eases and the ticks come faster. Small label: other inputs unchanged.
scenes.narration: Many nuclear cells fire steadily, like a car with its engine running. Ease off the brake, and the car speeds up.

scenes.tts: Here is the rule. The cerebellum learns to predict, and it learns from error.
scenes.visual: Rule card, line 1: The cerebellum learns to predict, and it learns from error.
scenes.narration: Here is the rule. The cerebellum learns to predict, and it learns from error.

scenes.tts: In this model, a well-timed error signal can weaken the parallel fibre synapses active at the right moment.
scenes.caption: In this model, a well-timed error signal can weaken the parallel-fibre synapses active at the right moment.
scenes.visual: Line 2 adds: A well-timed error signal can weaken the eligible parallel-fibre synapses. Small note under it: the timing window depends on the region; mouse flocculus, about 120 ms earlier. On the schematic, the blue synapses that fired in that window before the red spike dim.
scenes.narration: In this model, a well-timed error signal can weaken the parallel-fibre synapses active at the right moment.

scenes.tts: With other inputs unchanged, weaker input to the brake means more output there, the next time that context comes round.
scenes.visual: Line 3 adds: Weaker input to the brake means more output, at that point, next time. The brake eases and the nucleus ticks speed up at one point on a timeline.
scenes.narration: With other inputs unchanged, weaker input to the brake means more output there, the next time that context comes round.

scenes.tts: Parallel fibre activity without a paired climbing fibre can strengthen the same synapses. So corrections can run either way.
scenes.visual: Line 4 adds: Parallel-fibre activity without a paired climbing fibre can strengthen them; corrections run both ways. Arrows up and down on the synapse.
scenes.narration: Parallel-fibre activity without a paired climbing fibre can strengthen the same synapses. So corrections can run either way.
scenes.caption: Parallel-fibre activity without a paired climbing fibre can strengthen the same synapses. So corrections can run either way.

scenes.tts: This is the classical Marr Albus Ito model: well supported for some tasks, but not the whole story.
scenes.caption: This is the classical Marr-Albus-Ito model: well supported for some tasks, but not the whole story.
scenes.visual: Label beneath the rule card: Marr-Albus-Ito, the classical model. Well supported for some tasks; not the whole story.
scenes.narration: This is the classical Marr-Albus-Ito model: well supported for some tasks, but not the whole story.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: the cerebellum is a predictor, and errors are how it learns.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: A predictor that learns from error. Below it, smaller: Next: following the sign.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: the cerebellum is a predictor, and errors are how it learns.
